status_legend.SPEC-NOT-TESTED: Written, gate-mapped, and testable in principle - but no bet has been recorded and no result exists. This is the state of every strategy in this catalogue today.
status_legend.REJECTED-BY-GATE: Killed by a gate before any stake, on the record, so the reasoning is preserved and cannot be quietly retried.
status_legend.TRIAL-CANDIDATE: Eligible for a logged paper season once its data gap closes; still not fundable.

results_rule: Result columns are blank by design. Any number placed there must come from a stored, timestamped, settled bet ledger whose inputs satisfy gates G-01..G-04; filling them by estimate is what this catalogue exists to prevent.

strategies.name: Do-nothing benchmark (house hold)
strategies.hypothesis: Random selection at the market's prices loses the vig; every candidate strategy must beat this, not break even.
strategies.signal: No signal. Bet the same game and side as each candidate entry but at the closing price, with no model input.
strategies.edge: None claimed; this is the yardstick.
strategies.why_may_work: It reproduces exactly what an uninformed bettor experiences, so the loss rate is the cost of playing.
strategies.why_fails: It is not a strategy, and a candidate that merely matches it has no value.
strategies.gap: Needs the same price feed as everything else.

strategies.name: Our-line versus close: model-disagreement edge
strategies.hypothesis: If our originated number is better calibrated than the market on specific contexts, the discrepancy is the edge; if it is not, the discrepancy is noise - and the market close tells us which.
strategies.signal: Take the side when (our no-vig probability for that side) - (market no-vig probability at the cut-off) >= threshold, threshold fixed in the pre-registration; skip otherwise. Score primarily on closing-line value, not on wins.
strategies.stake: fractional Kelly, cap 0.5% bankroll per bet, sized on the modelled edge not the observed one
strategies.edge: Model information the market may underweight in specific contexts, measured against the close.
strategies.why_may_work: It is the only framework where 'the model was right' is separable from 'the team won'.
strategies.why_fails: Public closing lines are extremely informative; a decade-old academic comparison found opening and closing lines statistically similar in predictive value, i.e. little to harvest in the general case.
strategies.gap: No price feed (Q-01) and no originated line yet (R-07).

strategies.name: Total-first origination, then derive the spread
strategies.hypothesis: The total and the margin come from the same scoring process; pricing the total first and deriving the spread enforces internal consistency and exposes whichever market is off.
strategies.signal: Model expected points per possession for both teams -> expected total and expected margin; compare each to the market; trade the market with the larger standardised discrepancy, and never trade both against each other on the same game in the same cycle.
strategies.corr: two views of one game - the legs must not be combined into a parlay without a joint model (see the correlation page)
strategies.stake: fractional Kelly at the larger edge, halved when both markets disagree
strategies.edge: Internal consistency: the market prices the two legs with separate panels and separate flows.
strategies.why_may_work: Structural, not narrative: it is a no-arbitrage-ish relation rather than an opinion about a team.
strategies.why_fails: If our scoring model is biased, both markets are 'disagreeing' with our bias and the largest discrepancy is simply our worst error.
strategies.gap: Requires our own model (R-07) and prices (R-02).

strategies.name: Key-number value on half-point purchases
strategies.hypothesis: NFL margins pile up on 3 and 7, so moving a line across a key number has a step value that vig does not always cover; buying a half point is sometimes free and sometimes a rip-off.
strategies.signal: Compute win probability at each candidate line from our discrete margin distribution; act only when the value of the extra half point exceeds its vig cost by the registered margin, and only on the side of the key number where our model puts material mass.
strategies.stake: flat unit; sizing increases only after 3 seasons of stability
strategies.edge: A pricing asymmetry in the vig schedule rather than in opinions about teams.
strategies.why_may_work: It is arithmetic on the margin distribution; the distribution is estimable from official box scores alone, with no purchase required.
strategies.why_fails: Public knowledge of key numbers means the vig schedule already prices it; also our margin distribution could be wrong where it matters most.
strategies.gap: No proprietary pricing needed to build it - the missing piece is the historical price series to prove it.

strategies.name: Starting-QB availability shock
strategies.hypothesis: A confirmed change at the most important position moves true win probability more than the line adjusts in the time available, especially when the news lands after the bulk of the market's action.
strategies.signal: Trade only on the official report states (a QB listed Did Not Participate or Out/Doubtful, or a starter removed from a report he was on), against the price at the moment of the report, with a maximum allowed age of the information; no reporter rumours, no aggregate-site claims.
inputs: official report history per report day
strategies.corr: single leg per game; if two legs from the same game are wanted, they must be priced jointly
strategies.stake: fractional Kelly on the estimated shift, hard cap 1% of bankroll, no martingale chasing
strategies.edge: Speed plus the asymmetry that a practice report is public while its interpretation is not.
strategies.why_may_work: It is one of the few inputs where the market must reprice a hard fact rather than an opinion.
strategies.why_fails: Books reprice instantly, and the official report is deliberately coarse: a certain-to-play player is not listed in the game status at all, so 'absence' is not news, which is verified league policy, not a workaround.
strategies.gap: Report history is not collected yet (R-03); prices are absent (R-02).

strategies.name: Defensive-backfield depletion
strategies.market: team total, spread, opponent WR props
strategies.hypothesis: Cornerback depth is thin by roster construction; losing two top-cornerback bodies changes coverage quality more than a single-count 'out' list implies, and the line prices players, not depth charts.
strategies.signal: Deficiency index = sum over the secondary of (starter weight x availability penalty), where availability comes from the official report and the club depth chart's listed depth order; act when the index crosses a registered threshold and the opposing team's pass-market moves less than the index-implied shift.
inputs: per-position win-fraud baseline from our own model
strategies.corr: the team-total leg and the WR-prop leg in the same game are positively dependent by construction; combining them requires the joint model
strategies.edge: Depth-chart information that the line does not read directly, on the exact requirement in the brief about second and third-string replacements.
strategies.why_may_work: Positional asymmetry is real: a team can list one or two corners at all, which the fetched 49ers chart demonstrates (left cornerback has a single name on the chart).
strategies.why_fails: Coordinator adjustments (more safety rotation, more press from a nickel) can absorb the loss; the market may already know the practice report and price it.
strategies.gap: 32-club chart collection (SG-10) plus the causal impact estimate the repo cannot produce yet (Q-08).

strategies.name: Offensive-line depletion against the run game
strategies.market: opposing RB carries, team rush attempts, under on opponent pass attempts
strategies.hypothesis: Line-play availability shifts play distribution (more rushes, shorter downs) before it shifts scoring, so usage markets reprice later than side markets.
strategies.signal: Count unavailable interior linemen weighted by chart depth (a first-string guard and his only listed backup out is a different state from one reserve out); when the index crosses the threshold, take the usage side that our own projection model says is lagging, never the narrative side.
strategies.corr: multiple usage legs on the same team are strongly positively dependent; do not ticket them without the joint model
strategies.stake: 0.25% cap; props are low-liquidity and vig-heavy
strategies.edge: Usage-versus-scoring repricing lag on a market with fewer participants.
strategies.why_may_work: Prop books have thinner limits and fewer dedicated bettors than the sides market, so the same information moves prices less.
strategies.why_fails: Carry-counting and 'attempt' definitions are settled by the stats standard, not by our reading; a definitional mismatch turns a right bet into a lost ticket (Q-12).
strategies.gap: Prop price history (thinnest archive of all), plus verified stat definitions.

strategies.name: First-time-starter snap-share repricing
strategies.market: player receptions, rush attempts, fantasy-score props
strategies.hypothesis: When a replacement becomes a full-time participant, his usage jumps immediately while the line is still anchored to his historical per-game average, because props are set off volume expectations rather than snap projections.
strategies.signal: Detect a depth-chart promotion (position 1 changes between consecutive official club charts) or a DNP-by-a-starter pattern; take the OVER on the promoted player's volume prop when our projection of his snaps times per-snap production exceeds the line plus vig cost.
strategies.corr: receptions and receiving yards for the same player are highly positively dependent and must be priced jointly, not multiplied
strategies.stake: 0.25% cap, never both legs of a combo unless the joint price beats the operator's
strategies.edge: A lag between roster reality and the prop-setting anchor.
strategies.why_may_work: It uses only inputs that are public and dated, so it can be reconstructed honestly for past seasons if the charts are archived going forward.
strategies.why_fails: Snap-share data for the projection baseline is official only the day after games (verified league documentation), so the baseline itself is stale by construction; and prop books may already shade for the backup.
strategies.gap: Historic depth-chart archive does not exist yet - we can only start accumulating (Q-11).

strategies.name: Short-week and travel context on totals
strategies.hypothesis: Reduced preparation time and long resets suppress scoring pace, and the effect is more reliable than the market's uniform treatment of a short week.
strategies.signal: Only for the documented context states (Thursday game following a Sunday game, or an international-series game in the following week), act when our context-adjusted total differs from the market total by the registered amount and the market has not moved by the cut-off.
inputs: official schedule with kickoff and TV slots
strategies.corr: single leg; a game-total leg and a first-half-total leg from the same game must not be parlayed without a joint model
strategies.edge: A context term with a small, stable effect and few bettors specialising in it.
strategies.why_may_work: The repo already holds an official 2026 schedule with prime-time slots and international rows, so the context features need no new purchase; the effect is measurable from box scores alone.
strategies.why_fails: The effect is small, so it needs an enormous sample (a 1-2 point shift on a total is a fraction of a percent of win probability), and this is the classic place where a season of luck masquerades as an edge.
strategies.gap: No results possible without prices; the modelled part can be built now.

strategies.name: Availability-driven alternate-line consistency
strategies.hypothesis: Alternate lines are set by formula from the main line, so a large availability change can leave an internal inconsistency (a team-total alternate and its spread alternate implying different margins) rather than an opinion error.
strategies.signal: Compute the implied margin from the alternate spread and from the alternate team totals; when the implied difference exceeds the vig-cost-adjusted bound, take the inconsistent leg. Purely internal-arithmetic based.
inputs: alternate line prices across the ladder
strategies.corr: legs from the same ladder are nested, so their correlation is exact by construction (see correlation page) and they must never be parlayed together
strategies.stake: 0.25% cap; expect limits and voids on ladder bets
strategies.edge: Mechanical pricing of a ladder that is repriced less often than the main line.
strategies.why_may_work: It is checkable arithmetic, not a forecast; the failure mode is mostly 'the ladder was never really inconsistent'.
strategies.why_fails: Operators restrict ladder parlays and shrink limits precisely here; and a 'no-action' rule on a ladders market can void the winning leg.
strategies.gap: Needs ladder prices, which the documented vendor's market list does not include - a separate source question.

strategies.name: Structurally correlated SGP (team total + same-team skill position)
strategies.hypothesis: Some same-game leg pairs have dependence we can model well because both are driven by one latent variable (expected plays and efficiency for that team); operators price this with a correlation assumption we may be able to beat.
strategies.signal: Price the joint with our own two-dimensional model; enter only when our joint probability exceeds the operator's implied probability after removing vig, AND the pair's correlation is measured on our own history with an interval that excludes the operator's assumption.
inputs: SGP prices and the operator's correlation/repricing rules
our own resolved ticket history for the correlation
strategies.corr: the whole strategy is the correlation: an unmeasured pair is not eligible (Q-20)
strategies.stake: 0.25% cap, and never more than one SGP per game in the ledger
strategies.edge: Better dependence modelling than the default assumption in the boost.
strategies.why_may_work: Boosts are marketing: a boosted price can still be worse than fair, and knowing the real dependence is the way to tell.
strategies.why_fails: It cannot be tested in year one at all - it requires our own resolved tickets; and if the operator voids correlated combos, the ticket never settles as modelled (Q-07).
strategies.gap: Everything: joint model, SGP price capture, and a measured correlation.

strategies.name: Cross-game parlays with an explicit independence penalty
strategies.hypothesis: Cross-game parlay pricing assumes independence; games in the same week share league-wide information (rules, weather patterns, divisional scouting), so a modest dependence assumption should usually be enough to find the ticket that is not overpriced.
strategies.signal: Price the ticket as the product of marginal probabilities times an explicit dependence factor measured from our own resolved tickets (or set conservatively to 1.0 with the ticket then flagged as unverified-dependence); require the operator's implied probability to fall short of ours by the registered margin.
strategies.corr: dependence factor is the input; unmeasured means the ticket is logged but not funded
strategies.stake: 0.25% cap per ticket; total parlay exposure capped at 3% of bankroll
strategies.edge: The vig stack on parlays is only worth attacking when the legs are genuinely near-independent and each leg is a real bet.
strategies.why_may_work: A parlay of individually-value legs is a legitimate way to reduce per-bet cost if and only if the joint price does not double-charge vig.
strategies.why_fails: Most operators price the same legs worse in a parlay than as singles; if any leg pushes, non-SGP parlay rules can leave the ticket settled short, which changes the distribution we assumed (published in the operator rules we cite).
strategies.gap: Marginal prices (R-02) and the dependence measurement (needs resolved history).

strategies.name: Same-player prop combo priced from one latent distribution
strategies.market: receptions + receiving yards, rushing yards + rushing TDs
strategies.hypothesis: Two props on the same player are the same random variable viewed twice; pricing them from a single fitted distribution exposes combos the operator priced as if independent, and equally exposes the ones that are far worse.
strategies.signal: Model per-player volume with a truncated count distribution and yards-per-catch noise; enumerate the offered points; enter a combo only when the joint probability from our distribution exceeds the operator's implied probability after devigging, with the same distribution also required to reproduce each single-prop price within tolerance (self-consistency check).
strategies.corr: near-deterministic dependence; the correlation is the trade, and it must be declared with our fitted value and interval
strategies.stake: 0.25% cap; one combo per player per game
strategies.edge: A structural mispricing in how combos are built, not a forecast about a player.
strategies.why_may_work: Self-consistency between the singles and the combo is a falsifiable arithmetic condition, so the strategy tells us when it is wrong, not just when it wins.
strategies.why_fails: If our per-player distribution is wrong in its tail, both the singles and the combo are wrong together and the self-consistency check passes while the bet loses.
strategies.gap: Prop lines and the projection baseline (Q-11, Q-12).

strategies.name: Model-vs-market disagreement with CLV-only promotion
strategies.hypothesis: The promotion decision itself should be taken on closing-line value, because CLV is the only quantity in the system that measures whether we were better informed than the market rather than luckier than it.
strategies.signal: Score every candidate strategy by mean (our probability minus market-implied probability) at entry, and its t-statistic on the CLV distribution, with no use of game outcomes at all for promotion; outcomes are used only to confirm calibration and detect a broken settlement path.
strategies.corr: not applicable - it is a ranking rule, and it is the reason the leaderboard exists
strategies.stake: not a staking rule; a gate on staking
strategies.edge: Methodological: it removes the outcome lottery from the funding decision.
strategies.why_may_work: Widely used in professional practice because it needs a much smaller sample than PnL to detect a real edge.
strategies.why_fails: CLV is not the same as profit: a strategy can beat the close consistently and still lose on a market that is right for reasons outside our model; it also presumes we can capture the close, which is a data question with a cost.
strategies.gap: Requires the price capture at the cut-off, i.e. Q-01 and SG-07.

strategies.name: Last-season-over / 'team is due' regression to the market
strategies.hypothesis: Bettors systematically over-weight recent public narratives, so fading them finds value.
strategies.signal: PROPOSED SIGNAL: bet against the side with the higher public share after a streak of covering. Rejected before evaluation by the pre-registration gate.
inputs: public betting-share data we do not have
strategies.why_may_work: Nothing in the verified sources supports treating a narrative streak as a priced inefficiency.
strategies.why_fails: REJECTED: (1) it has no pre-registered data source - public-share figures are not available to us from an official source, so the signal could not be computed honestly; (2) it is the archetype of a luck-selected strategy from a large trial space; (3) the break-even arithmetic at -110 (52.38%) means an unsourced tilt of a few tenths is noise. Recorded here so it is not re-proposed as if it were new.

strategies.name: Follow a 'sharp' money flow signal from an unattributed source
strategies.hypothesis: Reproducing observed line moves tells us where informed money went.
strategies.signal: PROPOSED SIGNAL: enter when a move of 2+ points appears on a tracked panel. Rejected at the data-lineage gate.
strategies.why_fails: REJECTED: (1) violates the data-lineage gate - an alert we cannot timestamp to its source is not auditable, and this repository's rule is that an unverifiable value is blank, not borrowed; (2) by the time a public alert fires, our available price is already the moved price, so the edge is consumed by the time we can act; (3) the academic sample we cite found only about a tenth of games moved 2+ points, and moving with a lag is a cost, not an edge.
strategies.gap: None - the strategy is rejected on method.
